In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both approaches present some advantages and drawbacks, so that a final decision about which one is more adequate cannot be taken.
the directory-based architecture is the most suitable one to be used in dense CMP systems, although it must be carefully implemented.
the performance of both architectures depends on the application mix, and no single architecture is clearly better than the other one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the directory-based D-CMP architecture presents better performance, while the SBF D-CMP architecture is more suitable for those applications that do not require a high bandwidth between processors.
, although the SBF architecture presents a more efficient cache-coherence protocol, the directory-based one achieves a better overall performance.

the SBF architecture presents a good scalability in terms of the number of processor cores, and that the directory-based architecture presents a better performance in terms of average response times, but its scalability is limited by the number of processor caches that can be integrated in the L2 level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SBF and directory-based D-CMP architectures are not suitable for the same applications.
, for D-CMP systems, the performance achieved by a directory-based approach may not be as good as expected, and that a snoop-based approach can be a good alternative.
the SBF architecture, despite of the high performance that the bus fabric interconnection can offer, is not the best option when dealing with D-CMP architectures.
